memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said to Moses, "When you return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have given you the power to do. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go."" - Exodus 4:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the hardest verses in Exodus, and we should not rush past it. God says He will harden Pharaoh's heart.

A few things help us here. First, read the whole account. Exodus says God hardened Pharaoh's heart, and it also says Pharaoh hardened his own heart. Both are true, and Scripture holds them together without embarrassment. Pharaoh was never a puppet; he was a proud, cruel man doing exactly what he wanted to do.

Second, God is doing something judicial here. Pharaoh had already ordered the drowning of infants. God confirming a man in the direction he has freely chosen is judgement, not injustice. Paul discusses this very passage and reminds us we are in no position to answer God back (Rom 9:17-20).

Sincere believers have long differed on how divine sovereignty and human responsibility fit together, and this devotional will not settle that. What we can say with confidence is this: God is never the author of evil, no one is ever condemned unjustly, and God's purposes stand.

Take the warning seriously. Every time we resist God's voice, our hearts grow a little harder. Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your heart (Heb 3:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an area where I have been repeatedly resisting what God has made clear?
2. Am I willing to trust God's justice where I cannot fully understand His ways?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart soft toward You. Where I have been resisting, break through and give me a willing spirit. Amen.
